_readme: THE SEED THIS REPOSITORY BUILDS AGAINST. Read by Tools/fetch_seed.sh; written by hand.
Two rulings live in this file, and both of them are one line: `sha256`.
RULING A -- CI IS PINNED, AND A PUBLISH BUMPS THE PIN DELIBERATELY.
Tools/fetch_seed.sh used to resolve the seed from the LIVE bucket manifest, so the bytes CI
compiled against changed the moment anyone published. On 2026-08-22 that happened: the s17
publish moved manifest.json, every job on main started fetching a seed whose row counts no
SeedCorpus entry was pinned for, and main went red retroactively -- from a commit that had
been green, without a commit. PR #112 was the fix-forward. A publish must not be able to
break a tree that already passed, so the version the repository builds against is now a
checked-in fact, bumped in a pull request that also carries whatever constants move with it.
RULING B -- THE BUNDLE IS PINNED TO PRE-NYC SCOPE.
The same file is what the app bundles. The s17 fused seed is 706 MB (1,097,382 trees, three
id spaces), so the next build would have handed every tester a 706 MB app carrying five
boroughs they never asked for -- while the Cities screen offered those same boroughs as
downloads it would then refuse, because a bundled city is not offered (CityInstallState).
So the pin names the last fused seed built before New York: San Francisco and central San
Jose, 108,249,088 bytes. New York arrives the way it was designed to, as five borough packs
from the published format-2 manifest.
WHY THIS ARTIFACT AND NOT AN s17 REBUILD OF THE SAME SCOPE. Three reasons, in order:
* It exists, at a write-once path (R37.2), and no bucket write is needed to pin it.
* Nothing in the app reads s17's addition. `dim_region` and `trees.region_id` are the unit
Tools/publish_cities.py NARROWS a pack on; `SeedSchema.hasRegions` is introspected and
read by no query in Cypress/. An s16 bundle beside s17 packs is the configuration R37.3
describes and RegionGenerationTests is written against.
* An s17 rebuild of SF+SJ would also carry the 2026-08-22 re-read of both layers, which is
fresher CITY DATA in the app -- a change to what testers receive, and not what was ruled.
It is available to anyone who wants it: both cities publish packs at content_rev
2026-08-22, so the Cities screen offers the refresh as `bundledOutdated`.
HOW TO BUMP IT. Publish first, then, in the pull request that carries the publish round:
1. put the new build_id in `path` and `build_id`, and the new `sha256` and `bytes`;
2. re-state `schema_version`, `tree_count` and `id_spaces` from the file's own receipt --
Tools/fetch_seed.sh checks `id_spaces` against `seed_meta.id_spaces_in_file` and refuses
a mismatch, which is what stops a full-scope seed being pinned into the bundle by reflex;
3. add or update the CypressTests/SeedCorpus.swift entry for the new corpus, measured;
4. run the suite on the merged tree, as always.
Never widen a check here to make a red go away. A hash that does not match is the pin working.
WHAT EACH FIELD'S PROVENANCE IS, because they differ. `sha256` and `bytes` are measured off
the file. `tree_count` and `id_spaces` are the file's own receipt (`seed_meta.rows_kept` and
`seed_meta.id_spaces_in_file`). `schema_version` is DERIVED by introspection -- a fused seed
carries no version integer of its own, and 16 is what `SeedSchema` reads off this file:
`dim_city` present, `dim_region` absent. Only `id_spaces` is checked automatically; the other
two are recorded so a reader knows what they are pinning without opening 103 MB.
